The adapter must collect behavior evidence only from public Framerail, Deepwell, and WWS HTTP seams; use the standard Docker runtime-identity helper only for pre-run and post-run infrastructure identity; reconcile all four scoped cases exactly once; prove cleanup; and publish through the existing no-replace primitive.

A dedicated media runtime runner would duplicate existing identity, lifecycle, cleanup, and no-replace owners and is not an accepted solution.

a successful HTTP status without blob and actor identity

reusable_source.reuse: Keep the source-bound input identities, run-owned page lifecycle, exact reconciliation, and cleanup control in the existing generic runtime owner. Add only a file-action adapter; do not create a media-specific controller.
Validate a sealed, fresh, non-standing production candidate identity and its immutable image, source, FTML, configuration, endpoint, and evidence bindings.
Observe every declared candidate service before and after capture and reject container, image, label, health, mount, network, port, or effective-configuration drift.
Reuse candidate attachment, clean-source execution identity, request gating, pre/post runtime stability, and sealed terminal receipt patterns without reusing the fixed standing-canary case set.
Reuse the distinct DOMContentLoaded-immediate and settled capture ordering, resource completion, request-failure collection, and screenshot artifact identities.
Reuse the isolated browser context, non-standing local endpoint, request gate, proxy, service-worker block, and close-all-resources behavior.
Publish terminal plan, case, cleanup, and verdict artifacts without replacing an earlier candidate result.

do_not_reuse_as_acceptance.reason: It starts a mock XML-RPC fixture and a development Framerail preview instead of attaching to the sealed production candidate.
It may coordinate disposable stages, but its mutable state and summary files are not a no-replace terminal acceptance receipt and its generic command plan does not prove media behavior.

submit the multipart file action through the public Framerail HTTP seam and capture its exact serialized response

issue GET and HEAD for original and resized identities through the public WWS HTTP seam
public_behavior_oracle: Framerail action status and serialized response bytes
Deepwell page file inventory and action responses
WWS GET and HEAD status, headers, and body SHA-256
the external request events issued and observed by the adapter; no inference about server-internal order
missing_generic_seam.supplemental_state_role: Database and files inspection may prepare and clean the run-owned fixture and seal pre-run and post-run identity, but it cannot decide a case verdict.
missing_generic_seam.cleanup: Record every run-owned page, file, revision, and pending blob before use; remove or cancel them in normal, error, and signal paths; and prove their absence before terminal publication.

standard_candidate_infrastructure_identi.use: Observe Docker labels, immutable image IDs, effective configuration, loopback bindings, and service stability before and after the four public-HTTP cases.

terminal_publication_prerequisites: all four case IDs reconcile exactly once with no skipped or duplicate result
each verdict is computed from independently fixed inputs and public HTTP observations rather than a producer-authored pass value
the standard candidate infrastructure identity is stable after cleanup
the aggregate and case receipts are published through install/local/wikidot-verification/src/atomic-no-replace.mjs
rejected_substitutes: a dedicated open43 media runtime runner

missing_contracts.reason: The existing generic runtime owner has no file-action adapter for the four scoped runtime cases. This one adapter integration must bind the fixed byte and actor plan, task-owned fixture identity, run-owned page and file lifecycle, Framerail multipart serialization, Deepwell file actions and next reads, WWS original and resized GET or HEAD observations, external request events, cleanup absence, exact reconciliation, stable standard infrastructure identity, and no-replace publication. Direct DB or files access is permitted only for fixture setup, cleanup, and identity support, never as the pass oracle.

The candidate-only Playwright config and test do not exist. This separate browser owner still needs a source-owned plan for exact candidate URLs, media inputs, actor IDs, private storage-state hashes, run-owned browser state, and finally or signal cleanup. The standing canary runner captures fixed read-only pages and cannot substitute for icon transitions, media frames, Gallery viewer actions, or multipart upload workflows.

The reusable standing observation records request failures and HTTP error responses, but the media contract also requires console errors, page errors, the main response CSP header, securitypolicyviolation events, iframe request attempts, and fail-closed no-request intervals. These fields need a source-owned media observation contract rather than an assumed empty array.

The browser case requires an observed before/after icon-setting change, while M756_UPLOAD_MATERIALIZATION remains blocked_evidence for upload/download transaction, replacement, deletion, MIME, size, SVG/script, and failure semantics. The harness must not invent a mutation solely to make the browser row executable.

required_ownership_boundary.candidate_stack: external owner named by the sealed candidate identity; harness observes but does not build, start, stop, replace, or remove it
required_ownership_boundary.run_owned_state: generic file-action adapter; every created page, revision, file, and pending blob is recorded before use and removed or cancelled in normal, error, and signal paths
required_ownership_boundary.terminal_evidence: existing generic candidate controller; no-replace publication only after exact case reconciliation, cleanup absence, and stable post-run candidate observation
required_ownership_boundary.secrets: private operator inputs only; receipts contain actor and storage-state hashes but no credentials, session cookies, presigned URLs, or tokens

review.readiness_rule: Keep C_MEDIA_RUNTIME_CANDIDATE exists_now=false until the existing generic runtime differential owns the narrow file-action adapter, source-blind tests reject wrong bytes, wrong external request order, stale next reads, missing cleanup, identity drift, duplicate cases, and skipped cases, and the command targets that generic owner rather than a dedicated media runner. Keep C_MEDIA_BROWSER_CANDIDATE false until its separate browser contracts exist. A producer-authored pass value is never sufficient.

issues.title: Page file upload fails before blob commit

subrows.acceptance: Return successful and failed multipart actions without an arbitrary File object in SvelteKit's serialized payload.
subrows.reason: Source returns withFiles({ form, res }), which addresses the historical cause. The remaining candidate evidence needs the generic file-action adapter to submit the real public Framerail multipart action and verify its exact successful and failed serialized responses without using an internal object as the oracle.

subrows.acceptance: Check Page:Edit, then blob_upload, presigned PUT, and file_create in order, and expose the created file only after relation commit.
subrows.reason: The Framerail lifecycle test owns the internal Page:Edit, blob_upload, PUT, and file_create caller order; the candidate must not infer those internal calls. The remaining candidate evidence needs the generic file-action adapter to submit the public action, record only external requests it issues and observes, and prove the public next read exposes the file only after the action commits while failed actions expose no file.

evidence_partition.source_owned: framerail/tests/page-file-upload-lifecycle.test.js records the internal Deepwell caller order, and framerail/tests/presigned-upload.test.js proves file commit cannot run before an accepted PUT.
evidence_partition.candidate_owned: The generic file-action adapter submits the public Framerail action and verifies its response plus the next public Deepwell inventory and WWS bytes. It records only its own external request events and does not claim visibility into Framerail-to-Deepwell internal traffic.

subrows.acceptance: Require parent-page edit permission and exact site/page/blob ownership; reject client authority over another pending blob.
subrows.reason: blob_upload now derives page ownership from the trusted request context, the database enforces scoped-or-unscoped shape, and typed page finalization rejects another actor, page, site, or unscoped pending blob without exposing whether the token exists. The public endpoint case proves the successful file_create response and subsequent page_get_files/file_get bytes, with direct database access limited to supplemental ownership-persistence, fixture-setup, and cleanup assertions.
existing_tests: install/local/wikidot-verification/tests/corpus-import-attachments.test.mjs::materializeCorpusRowAttachments binds pending uploads to the trusted page context

subrows.acceptance: On presign, PUT, timeout, or file_create failure, create no file relation, leave no public route, cancel pending state, and preserve list/cache state.
subrows.reason: Every page-scoped upload caller now owns the same failure boundary: the Framerail form flow and XML-RPC bridge share a pending upload lifecycle, while the corpus importer applies the same sequence at its process boundary. After pending allocation, PUT, file_create, or file_edit failure triggers exactly one separate blob_cancel request with the original actor, site, and page context; cleanup failure is suppressed so the original failure remains authoritative, and successful commits are not cancelled. Focused Node cases prove order, context, exactly-once cleanup, original-error preservation, and success behavior. The XML-RPC fixture independently requires exact page-scoped params plus session/site/page headers. The Deepwell public ownership case proves failed commits expose no file relation and now guarantees global pending-row and DB/S3 fixture cleanup after an assertion or teardown panic; direct DB/S3 access remains test-only setup and cleanup. A task-owned runtime candidate still must prove transport timeout, cache, and object-store behavior.
